paper.title_en: Relating Short Range Correlated Pair Abundances to Electron-Scattering Cross Section Ratios
paper.abstract_en: We derive a coupled set of relations between inclusive and semi-exclusive nucleon-knockout electron-scattering cross-section ratios measured for any two nuclei in short-range-correlation (SRC) kinematics and the microscopic neutron-proton, (np-), proton-proton (pp-), and neutron-neutron (nn-) SRC pair populations in those nuclei. The derivation uses a factorized description of quasielastic scattering from SRC pairs and includes final-state interactions through nuclear transparency and single charge exchange. We show that the inclusive $(e,e')$, proton-knockout $(e,e'p)$, and neutron-knockout $(e,e'n)$ ratios are not independent: for any two nuclei where one is isospin symmetric ($N=Z$), two of these three observables determine the third within the model. For $^\mathrm{48}\mathrm{Ca}$ and $^\mathrm{40}\mathrm{Ca}$, for example, the measured inclusive $(e,e')$ and proton-tagged $(e,e'p)$ ratios predict $^\mathrm{48}\mathrm{Ca}/^\mathrm{40}\mathrm{Ca}(e,e'n)=1.35\pm0.07\,(\mathrm{exp})\pm0.15\,(\mathrm{model})$. A measurement of the $(e,e'n)$ ratio therefore provides a direct consistency test of the factorized pair-counting description. It also constrains the single-charge-exchange probabilities. Combining all three ratios with the two double-coincidence ratios determines the relative np-, pp-, and nn- SRC pair populations of any two nuclei. If one nucleus is isospin symmetric, any two of the three ratios suffice for the same result.
